text:
Tony DeAngelo has always been a trade: offense from the blue line, with a defensive bill attached. With the Islanders this season the offense is there and the bill is smaller than usual, at least so far.

He has 2 goals and 6 assists in 21 games, and his ice time over his last ten is up 2.8 minutes to 19.2 a night. New York is even at five-on-five with him on, 50% of the expected goals. Last season Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on the ice than against nearly any defenseman (bottom 1%), so even is progress.

He should have more points. The Islanders have scored 4.9 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on, and we flag him as due for that to swing back. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows why he gets power-play time: 6.3 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 91st percentile among defensemen. It also shows the weak spot: only 29% of his exits kept possession.

Off the scoresheet, he had a brief moment in the headlines when Corey Perry, at 41, dropped the gloves with him against the Kings.
headline: Points, and the price of them
